source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS), Final Fiscal Year 2025, Table 9, Summary of Receipts and Outlays by Function (net outlays, fiscal-year-to-date through 2025-09-30).
sourceShort: Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement, Final FY2025 (Table 9)
note: Net outlays. Some functions can be net-negative (accounting offsets that reduce total spending), shown as credits on the receipt. The functions sum exactly to totalOutlays.

categories.name: Social Security
categories.explainer: Monthly retirement, survivor, and disability benefits for workers and their families. Funded mainly by the payroll taxes shown separately in your tax breakdown.

categories.name: Medicare
categories.explainer: Health coverage for Americans age 65+ and some younger people with disabilities. Partly funded by the Medicare payroll tax shown separately.

categories.name: Health
categories.explainer: Health spending other than Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, public health, NIH research, and ACA subsidies.

categories.name: Net Interest
categories.explainer: Interest the government pays on the national debt, minus interest it earns. This buys no services today, it is the cost of past borrowing.

categories.name: National Defense
categories.explainer: Military personnel and operations, weapons procurement, and defense research, primarily the Department of Defense.

categories.name: Income Security
categories.explainer: Support for basic needs: unemployment insurance, SNAP (food assistance), housing aid, refundable tax credits, and federal employee retirement.

categories.name: Veterans Benefits and Services
categories.explainer: Health care, disability compensation, pensions, and education benefits for military veterans and their families.

categories.name: Transportation
categories.explainer: Highways, mass transit, aviation and air traffic control, railroads, and maritime programs.

categories.name: Natural Resources and Environment
categories.explainer: National parks and public lands, the EPA, conservation, water resources, and pollution control.

categories.name: Administration of Justice
categories.explainer: Federal law enforcement (FBI, DEA), the federal courts, prisons, and immigration enforcement.

categories.name: Community and Regional Development
categories.explainer: Disaster relief and recovery, community and rural development, and regional economic programs.

categories.name: Education, Training, Employment, and Social Services
categories.explainer: Student financial aid, K-12 grants, job training, and social services. (FY2025 reflects large student-loan accounting adjustments.)

categories.name: Agriculture
categories.explainer: Farm income support, crop insurance, and agricultural research and conservation.

categories.name: International Affairs
categories.explainer: Diplomacy and embassies, foreign economic and humanitarian aid, and international security assistance.

categories.name: General Science, Space, and Technology
categories.explainer: NASA, the National Science Foundation, and basic scientific research across federal agencies.

categories.name: General Government
categories.explainer: The cost of running the federal government itself, the IRS, central management, legislative and executive operations.

categories.name: Energy
categories.explainer: The electric grid, energy research, strategic reserves, and nuclear-site cleanup.

categories.name: Commerce and Housing Credit
categories.explainer: Housing finance, the Postal Service, and commerce programs. Can be net-negative when loan repayments and fees exceed outlays, it reduces total spending.

categories.name: Undistributed Offsetting Receipts
categories.explainer: Accounting offsets subtracted from totals, chiefly agencies' payments into federal retirement funds and royalties from resources on public land.
